text:
nightly-bot: nightly eval report: quantized-v1 (q8_0) — regression: +3.2% failures on prompt-set dialogue-safety vs baseline. Artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/ev/1778004321

sophia: saw this early this morning. lots of repetition/looping in outputs when temp=0.9. Example: "Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes..." flagged as semantic-breakdown.

maria: did we change sampling defaults? I thought temp/top_p stayed the same.

kevin: we didn't change the defaults, but the continuous-batching patch altered RNG stream assignment. That can change sequences even if params identical.

ryan: good call. could also be a bug in top_p+temp interaction — I remember an edge-case where scaling happened before top_p truncation.

sophia: I'll try to reproduce deterministically. running small harness with explicit seed.

sophia: command I'm using: 
```bash
run_eval --model quantized-v1 --prompt-set dialogue-safety --temp 0.9 --top_p 0.95 --top_k 0 --seed 42 --num_samples 50 --output /tmp/run42.json
```

sophia: quick raw diff from baseline run (seed 42 baseline vs nightly): 50 samples -> 12 failures baseline, 27 failures nightly. Attaching two example generations in thread.

maria: hmm. if same seed diverges, that's a strong signal RNG stream ordering changed (batch boundary/non-deterministic scheduling). But also check whether temperature is applied twice.

kevin: I instrumented the runtime locally. When top_p < 1 and we run the new batched path, we call temperature_scale(logits) then compute top_p mask, but later a helper that normalizes logits also applies a scale when it expects unscaled logits. Repro: apply temp=0.9 twice -> increased mode collapse.

ryan: can you paste the small snippet where it happens?

kevin: snippet: 
```python
# simplified
logits = model_step(...)
logits = logits / temp    # applied here in new path
mask = top_p_mask(logits)
probs = softmax(masked_logits / temp)  # accidental second scaling
```

kevin: opening PR with fix + unit test now. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/2345

maria: thanks. add test for temp=1 (no-op), temp<1 and top_p in {0.8,0.95} and seed stability across batch sizes.

ryan: meanwhile let's pin sampling configs in nightly eval to the exact pre-change harness and include seed param so we can triage quicker. sophia, can you queue that?

sophia: pinned nightly eval: added flags --seed 42 --pin-sampling-config /configs/sampling/pre-batching.json. Re-run queued (job 1778004380).

sophia: re-run finished: failures back to 13/50 (close to baseline) when using pinned config. When running with current runtime (no PR) and same seed, failures 26/50.

kevin: PR #2345 includes: remove duplicate temp scaling, add deterministic RNG stream assignment for continuous batching, and a regression test. Assigning reviewers @maria @ryan.

maria: reviewing now, small docstring nit. Also let's add an integration test that runs 100 short prompts with/without batching to assert identical outputs with fixed seed.

ryan: agreed. After merge, we should unblock nightly and run a 1k-sample smoke eval to be safe. Also add a dashboard card showing failure rate vs sampling params (temp/top_p/top_k).

sophia: merge looks good locally — retest in canary once PR is in. Keeping nightly blocked until canary passes. :lock:

kevin: PR merged (2345) -> canary build queued 1778004480.

sophia: canary results: canary run shows failures 12/50, matches baseline. Rolling nightly back on.

ryan: great. follow-ups: (1) add explicit seed to nightly forever, (2) add param-sensitivity eval, (3) audit other helpers for duplicate scaling.

maria: filing backlog ticket for audit. Tagging infra to watch for RNG assumptions in other optimizations.

kevin: thanks all. lesson: sampling math + batching + RNG ordering = subtle nondets.

sophia: closing thread when dashboards update. :white_check_mark:
